france24fr.title: ONU : Antonio Guterres plaide pour un siège permanent de l'Afrique au Conseil de sécurité

spiegel.title: Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang und Donald Trump: Der KI-Einflüsterer
spiegel.description: Jensen Huang leitet Nvidia, das wertvollste Unternehmen der Welt. Von KI-Horrorszenarien hält er nichts – so ist er zum wichtigen Verbündeten von Donald Trump geworden. Doch hinter der Bromance steckt noch mehr.

spiegel.title: Äthiopien: Rebellen bringen Flughafen in Tigray unter ihre Kontrolle
spiegel.description: Der schwelende Konflikt zwischen der Volksbefreiungsfront von Tigray und der äthiopischen Zentralregierung flammt wieder auf, die Kämpfer haben einen Regionalflughafen eingenommen. Die Sorge vor einem neuen Bürgerkrieg ist groß.

spiegel.title: Grevenbroich: Kugelbombe in der Nähe von Strommast im Rheinland gefunden
spiegel.description: Sprengstoffexperten haben einen Feuerwerkskörper entschärft, der nur wenige Meter von einem Hochspannungsmast entdeckt worden war. Die Polizei prüft einen möglichen Zusammenhang zu früheren Sabotageakten.

spiegel.title: Jurassica Parka: Prozess gegen die Dragqueen wegen Besitz von Missbrauchsbildern von Kindern
spiegel.description: Als Kunstfigur Jurassica Parka war Mario O. eine Größe im Berliner Nachtleben. Privat konsumierte er Missbrauchsbilder von Kindern. Deshalb stand er nun vor Gericht – und legte ein Geständnis ab.

spiegel.title: Mini-AKW: Katherina Reiche wirbt für Atomenergie – nun entzaubern ihre Leute kleine Kernkraftwerke
spiegel.description: Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche sieht großes Potenzial in Mini-AKW. Doch laut einem vertraulichen Dokument, das dem SPIEGEL vorliegt, zweifeln ihre eigenen Fachleute daran. Der bislang von ihr propagierte Hauptvorteil existiert demnach noch nicht.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt/Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Johannes stimmte für die AfD, Lea für die Linke
spiegel.description: Bei den Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern taten sich viele junge Menschen schwer. Wir haben mit ihnen gesprochen.

spiegel.title: Somalia: Nach Dürre nun Flut – Hunderttausende Menschen in Gefahr
spiegel.description: In Somalia herrscht seit rund einem Jahr Dürre, Millionen Menschen hungern. Nun könnte das Klimaphänomen El Niño zusätzlich verheerende Fluten auslösen, warnt Jan Egeland, Chef des Norwegischen Flüchtlingsrats.

spiegel.title: Serie »Brothers« mit Matthew McConaughey und Woody Harrelson: Betuliche Bromance
spiegel.description: Betuliche Bromance: Matthew McConaughey und Woody Harrelson spielen in »Brothers« sich selbst. Sind die beiden wirklich Halbbrüder, wie ein Gerücht behauptet? Unterhaltsame Frage, aber nicht über acht Folgen.

spiegel.title: Österreich will Spritpreise um zwölf Cent senken
spiegel.description: Der Blick auf die Preisanzeige an österreichischen Tankstellen könnte bald etwas weniger Stress auslösen. Die Regierung plant eine Preisbremse für zwei Monate – um die Menschen »zukunftsfroh« zu stimmen.

spiegel.title: Bier, Boobs und Brezn: Die erste lesbische Party auf dem Oktoberfest ist ein politischer Akt wider Willen
spiegel.description: Bier, Brüste und Brezeln verspricht das erste lesbische Wiesn-Event. In Wahrheit geht es um viel mehr.

spiegel.title: Oktoberfest 2026 in München: Die Wiesn ist ein Ort, an dem sich Täter sicher fühlen
spiegel.description: Wie gefährlich ist die Wiesn für Frauen? Die Sozialarbeiterin Kristina Gottlöber betreut im »Safe Space« Frauen und Mädchen in Notlagen. Hier erklärt sie, warum es so viele Übergriffe gibt.

spiegel.title: US-Midterms: OSZE erstmals nicht zur Wahlbeobachtung in die USA eingeladen
spiegel.description: Bei den Midtermwahlen in den USA werden zum ersten Mal seit 2002 keine europäischen Beobachter anwesend sein. Die OSZE sieht darin eine »deutliche Abkehr von einer bewährten demokratischen Praxis«.

spiegel.title: Gesundheitssystem: Ende der Privatversicherung? So hat Friedrich Merz das doch nicht gemeint
spiegel.description: Der neue Gesundheitsminister Carsten Linnemann muss im Bundestag erklären, was Friedrich Merz mit seinen Äußerungen zum deutschen Gesundheitssystem bezwecken wollte. Keine leichte Aufgabe.

spiegel.title: Berliner Linke: Gysi warnt vor CDU-Koalition – Throm will Beobachtung durch Verfassungsschutz prüfen
spiegel.description: Auf Initiative der AfD kamen Abgeordnete aller Fraktionen zu einer Aussprache im Bundestag zusammen. Thema: der Antisemitismusverdacht in der Berliner Linken. Von allen Seiten hagelte es Kritik.

spiegel.title: Berlin-Wahl 2026: Die Grünen sollten diesen Linken nicht zur Macht verhelfen
spiegel.description: In Berlin haben die Grünen starke Verluste erlitten. Nun wollen sie eine Koalition mit einer Linken, in deren Reihen Antisemitismus salonfähig wurde. Die Partei würde sich damit auch selbst schaden.

spiegel.title: Linke in Berlin: Elif Eralps Traum vom Roten Rathaus könnte platzen – wegen ein paar Genossen
spiegel.description: Ein Chat mit einer arabischstämmigen Clangröße, Fotos mit einem Terrorunterstützer: Radikale Linke aus Berlin-Neukölln haben düstere Verbindungen. Parteifreunde von Wahlsiegerin Elif Eralp scheinen die Machtübernahme zu sabotieren.

spiegel.title: Hendrik Holt: Windkraftbetrüger in Dubai festgenommen
spiegel.description: Er hat unter anderem Windparks verkauft, die es gar nicht gab, an ausländische Stromkonzerne. Der Prozess gegen Hendrik Holt sorgte deutschlandweit für Aufsehen – und auch seine Flucht. Jetzt ist er gefasst.

spiegel.title: Berlin-Wahl 2026: Frühere SPD-Bürgermeister Müller und Momper warnen vor Verhandlungen mit Linkspartei
spiegel.description: Michael Müller und Walter Momper regierten einst die Hauptstadt, nun raten sie von Sondierungen mit der Linken ab. Der Wahlabend habe gezeigt, »dass sich die Linkspartei mit Antisemiten und Clangrößen gemeinmacht«

observador.title: Alianza Ceibo ganha Gulbenkian para a Humanidade
observador.description: Povos indígenas da Amazónia premiados com um milhão de euros alertam para ameaças do extrativismo e da crise climática nos seus territórios.

observador.title: Consulta pública de metro de Gondomar teve 84 participações
observador.description: O EIA da linha entre o Estádio do Dragão e o Souto foi a consulta pública. A linha de 6,9 km, com custo até 163,8 M€, prevê 10,3 milhões de passageiros no 1.º ano.

observador.title: Andrea Lima: “O que nos une é pensar saúde, não é pensar ...
observador.description: Andrea Lima, do Fórum Saúde XXI, prepara o Cascais International Health Forum 2026, sobre longevidade, onde “Portugal pode perfeitamente ser um case-study europeu”. Vem aí “a sociedade dos 100 anos!”

observador.title: 20h. Zelensky já discursou na assembleia geral da ONU
observador.description: Zelensky começou o discurso a dizer que a perda de controlo da indústria petrolífera por parte da Rússia é "humilhante". Ainda, a comissão de inquérito a Luís Neves vai avançar.

observador.title: Ramos-Horta desafia Trump para cimeira nuclear em Portugal
observador.description: O Presidente timorense discursou na Assembleia-Geral da ONU e pediu ao líder dos EUA que seja "audacioso" e "visionário" no combate à proliferação nuclear.

observador.title: Mulher de 87 anos despejada em Madrid à quarta tentativa
observador.description: Foi o quarto — e definitivo — despejo em 7 anos. Uma lei da ditadura de Franco ditou o fim do contrato que a família tinha desde 1956. Empresa imobiliária quis aumentar renda de 500 para 2.650 euros.

observador.title: Jovem de 15 anos morre em acidente de trotinete
observador.description: O alerta foi dado às 15h28 desta quarta-feira, na freguesia de Boim. A vítima foi transportada com vida para o hospital de Penafiel, mas não resistiu.

observador.title: Pais acusam escola de Sintra de "abafar" maus-tratos
observador.description: Mães denunciaram "gritos constantes", castigos e agressões a um aluno autista. A direção da escola abriu "averiguação" e garante não haver indícios. Mas a coordenação pedagógica sabia dos relatos.

observador.title: Comissão de inquérito a Neves avança. Chega aceita mudanças
observador.description: Presidente da Assembleia da República pediu que duas das questões que seriam investigadas caíssem e Ventura aceitou. Maior parte do requerimento do Chega foi aceite.

observador.title: Crónica: Jorge, já fazes falta, pá
observador.description: As canções de Jorge Palma acompanharam-nos quando ainda não sabíamos que precisávamos delas. Agora, sobram as palavras, as músicas, as memórias e a estrada.

observador.title: Filho do embaixador de Israel nos EUA ferido na Cisjordânia
observador.description: Neria Leiter, o filho do embaixador de Israel nos EUA, ficou gravemente ferido num ataque com um carro na Cisjordânia, esta quarta-feira. Embaixador diz que o filho "precisa de um milagre".

observador.title: CML aprova 33,8 milhões para Web Summit e turismo
observador.description: Câmara de Lisboa aprovou financiamentos com votos da maioria PSD/CDS-PP/IL e Chega. Oposição criticou modelo de gestão das receitas da taxa turística.

observador.title: SEP denuncia contratos ilegais de 40 horas em Misericórdia
observador.description: Sindicato acusa instituição de impor 40 horas em vez das 35 do CCT e de obrigar deslocações às Minas da Panasqueira. Provedor fala em "bom senso" e deveres dos trabalhadores.

observador.title: As buscas na PJ ameaçam a credibilidade da instituição?
observador.description: Uma operação de buscas na Polícia Judiciária adensa a crise interna. Ainda, as medidas para conter a inflação amortecem a crise ou aumentam o risco orçamental?

observador.title: Portugal "muito bem" nas reservas de combustível
observador.description: França com 17% dos postos sem pelo menos um combustível. Maria da Graça Carvalho garante que Portugal está acima dos 90 dias recomendados e pede consciência no consumo.

observador.title: 19h. Avança a CPI a mandato de Luís Neves na liderança da PJ
observador.description: Aguiar Branco deu luz verde a 9 das 11 alíneas que o Chega quer investigar e André Ventura aceitou a decisão. Ainda, na próxima semana deve ser assinado um acordo no âmbito da nova fábrica de munições

observador.title: O caos na PJ pode ser uma tentativa para a denegrir?
observador.description: Vítor Alexandre vê o caos na PJ como resposta política de grupos poderosos. A PGR confirmou buscas na Judiciária, que podem resultar na constituição de Carlos Cabreiro como arguido, diz Luís Rosa.

observador.title: DJ, PR e PM: a escola inaugurada só por 175.000€

elpais.description: El empleado ha explicado que lo ha accionado accidentalmente al limpiarlo a petición de la diputada del partido

elpais.description: La última comida del día se adelanta en las reservas de los restaurantes, y también en las casas. ¿Por qué cenábamos tan tarde y por qué estamos dejando de hacerlo?

elpais.title: Best in Travel 2027: los mejores destinos para el año que viene (uno es español), según Lonely Planet
elpais.description: La editorial viajera anuncia su lista anual de lugares de todo el mundo, sugerencias y recomendaciones para descubrir los mejores rincones del planeta. nyt.title: Iran Will Not Be Bullied, President Masoud Pezeshkian Says in U.N. Speech

nyt.title: As Xi Visits Washington, Trump Plays Down China’s Actions Against U.S. Interests
nyt.description: Despite the rivalry between the United States and China, President Trump has repeatedly found ways to give President Xi Jinping of China a pass, portraying him more as a personal friend than a competitor.

nyt.title: Where Is the U.S. Beating China on A.I., and Where Is It Lagging?
nyt.description: As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, his country lags behind the United States on A.I. development in key areas — but Beijing has advantages elsewhere.

nyt.title: What’s Behind Bessent’s Boasts About the U.S. Bond Market
nyt.description: By one measure, U.S. government bond markets have posted negative returns, but markets in others countries have experienced steeper losses.

nyt.title: Disney’s Fired C.E.O. Bob Chapek Settles Scores With Bob Iger in New Book

npr.description: As President Trump and China's President Xi prepare to meet, Rush Doshi of the Council on Foreign Relations explains the current state of U.S.-China relations and what to expect from this summit.

npr.title: Greetings from Edinburgh, where a cheeky tour guide makes art history hilarious
npr.description: For anyone who grew up staring blankly at museum artwork, this is the fun that was missing: Coco leads interactive and (mostly) factual art history comedy tours.

npr.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
npr.description: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.

npr.title: Dems have an edge over GOP, poll finds. And, ICE looks into 'mobile detention centers'

npr.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met President Trump at the U.N. and proposed that Ukraine and Russia stop attacking each other's energy systems.

phys-org.title: Two new reports show that Canada needs to do much more to tackle climate change
phys-org.description: Global warming is expected to cross the 1.5°C temperature threshold—the lower limit of the Paris Agreement temperature goal—within a handful of years. This temperature increase shows no signs of slowing, and on our current trajectory, Canada is likely to experience temperatures 5°C above preindustrial levels by the end of the century.

phys-org.title: Study reveals how biological echo chambers form—and what can break them
phys-org.description: Tropical army ants are known to form devastating armadas that march through forests eating other insects and small creatures. As they march, they deposit chemical trails of pheromones that others behind them sense and follow. But occasionally one of these ants will walk in a circle, prompting a subset of ants behind them to follow until they all collapse and die.

A study led by an international team of researchers, including University of New Mexico paleobiologist Corinne "Cori" Myers, found that Earth's climate over the past 539 million years tended to remain within a small number of recurring climate states. phys-org.description: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit around Earth on Sept. 19, marking another milestone for an observatory that continues to transform our understanding of the universe.

phys-org.title: Making sense of shallow-water waves with advanced statistics
phys-org.description: When ocean waves reach shallow water, their complex interactions can produce lower-frequency infragravity waves. These waves strongly affect—and are affected by—the shape of coastlines, linking them to erosion, sediment deposition and the degradation of coastal ice.

phys-org.title: Natural compound from soil bacteria offers new approach to treating drug-resistant tuberculosis
phys-org.description: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than 10 million people contract tuberculosis (TB) each year. It is one of the deadliest infectious diseases worldwide. Treatment is lengthy and typically involves a combination of several antibiotics over many months. Drug-resistant strains are particularly problematic because the antibiotics used against them are only partially effective. New compounds capable of overcoming existing resistance are urgently needed.

phys-org.title: Reinvestigation of 6,800-year-old site in Serbia reveals larger settlement and egalitarian social structure
phys-org.description: Southeastern Europe and the Balkans are a key region for understanding the European Neolithic. Many ways of life and economic systems that continue to shape our lives today first emerged there in Europe and later spread across the continent. An archaeological culture named after the Vinča site in present-day Serbia marks a late phase of the Neolithic period in the region. phys-org.title: It's the small things: Treating something as even slightly significant affects motivation

phys-org.description: Microorganisms regulate key processes in soils and aquifers, including nutrient cycling, carbon turnover and contaminant degradation. Many bacteria use chemotaxis, the ability to sense and swim toward chemical signals, to locate nutrient-rich hotspots. However, natural subsurface environments are highly heterogeneous, containing complex pore networks that create strong variations in fluid flow and nutrient availability. phys-org.title: Workers with psychological capital are better prepared to weather increasing work stress

phys-org.title: Uncovering gravity's impact on the human genome
phys-org.description: The Human Genome Project was launched in 1990, preceded by decades of breakthroughs in genetics. It eventually gave us a sequence of the human genome. Yet, while the physical rules behind the genome's organization remain an active area of research, many questions are still largely unanswered. Among these is the impact of an omnipresent force influencing life on Earth: gravity.

phys-org.title: The far side of the moon provides clues to a past magnetic field
phys-org.description: Unlike Earth, the moon no longer has a core-generated magnetic field. On our planet, the movement of liquid iron in the outer core generates a global magnetic field. This so-called geodynamo works on a similar principle to a bicycle dynamo, which converts mechanical motion into electrical energy. "Today, there is an ongoing heated debate as to whether the moon also operated a dynamo in the past," says Xi Yang, a Ph.D. student in the Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences at ETH Zurich. This

phys-org.title: Brain organoids uncover how primates develop different brain shapes
phys-org.description: Most primate species have relatively large brains with surfaces marked by pronounced bulges and furrows. This is not the case with common marmosets (Callithrix jacchus). The brains of these small monkeys are smooth and virtually unfolded.

phys-org.title: Past emissions from top polluters will keep the planet warmer for decades to come
phys-org.description: If someone leaves the faucet running in your bathroom and the house floods, it's easy to assign responsibility for the damage. But for other disasters—bigger, more complicated and costlier ones—the link between cause and effect isn't as clear.

phys-org.title: Kibble with microbial proteins appeals to cats and dogs in new study
phys-org.description: In a new study, cats and dogs showed a short-term preference for kibble containing some protein derived from microorganisms over kibble containing only standard animal-derived protein. Ally Motta de Matos and A.L.B. Cruz of MicroHarvest—an European company that produces protein ingredients through fermentation, with pet food as its first market—present these findings in the open-access journal PLOS One.

phys-org.title: A horse named Pea is first to test focused ultrasound treatment of skin tumors called sarcoids
phys-org.description: There is no "one-fix-for-all" solution for sarcoids, said Sophie Bogers, an assistant professor of large animal surgery. Many require chemotherapy or invasive surgery. But she wants a better solution.

phys-org.title: Hormone-disrupting chemicals found in range of natural and drinking water sources
phys-org.description: A new study has found that chemicals that can affect fertility and reproductive health are contaminating natural and drinking water supplies. The researchers involved in the study have also developed a tool to help detect them. They analyzed samples from natural waterways, tap water, bottled water, tank water and rainwater and found hormone-disrupting substances—estrogenic endocrine-disrupting chemicals—in many of them. The research is published in the journal iScience.

phys-org.title: Exercise keeps astronauts' hearts strong enough for flight to Mars
phys-org.description: Intense exercise during long spaceflights helps maintain heart structure and function within a range needed to tolerate the low-gravity environment of Mars, a study co-led by a UT Southwestern Medical Center researcher suggests. The findings, published in Circulation, not only address an issue critical to future space missions but could also lead to better interventions to improve heart health on Earth.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: How Trade Deals Can Save Nature
proj-syn.description: Environmental conservation is among the most important, universally shared imperatives the world faces, and market access is one of the few carrots available in international politics. By linking tariffs to deforestation, the EU and others can create trade agreements that deliver more conservation and more gains from trade.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Third Way on China
proj-syn.description: Instead of choosing between a confrontation with China and business as usual, European policymakers should examine the benefits and costs of trade sector by sector to identify where mutually beneficial arrangements remain possible. Economic modeling shows that pragmatism beats more extreme options in most cases.

proj-syn.title: Alarm Bells in the Balkans
proj-syn.description: Recent developments in the Balkans ought to be a wake-up call for Europe, given the potential for nationalist provocations in one country to spill over within the region. Multiple elections coming next month raise the risk of a dangerous descent into political instability.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s 21st-Century Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Since his return to the White House, Donald Trump has turned his back on the free-market principles that the United States spent decades championing. In doing so, he threatens to dismantle the economic order that helped produce unprecedented growth in global output and trade.

proj-syn.title: The AI Productivity Delusion
proj-syn.description: As with previous technological revolutions, it is natural to focus on AI's net effects: Will it create more than it destroys? But unlike previous eras of creative destruction, the real question this time is, “Create more of what?”

proj-syn.title: Technological Leapfrogging in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Across Africa, past success stories have led policymakers to believe that developing economies can usually bypass the arduous, expensive stages of infrastructure development by adopting technologies built elsewhere. But this approach deserves more scrutiny, especially when applied to imported AI systems.

proj-syn.title: Preventing an AI World War
proj-syn.description: Warnings that AI may lead to our extinction often overlook the most immediate risk: a war triggered by an attack that no human intended or approved. A mechanism for distinguishing unintended harm from deliberate attacks is urgently needed.

proj-syn.title: Post-Liberal Europe?
proj-syn.description: Another victory for the far right in a German state election has confirmed European liberals' worst fears. With many critical European elections approaching in 2027, debates about the proper limits of popular sovereignty and other fundamental tenets of liberalism are now of paramount importance.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Moment of Reckoning
proj-syn.description: As its growth model runs out of road, Germany must decide whether to defend aging industries or enable new ones to emerge. To translate its research excellence into globally competitive companies, it needs deeper capital markets and a genuine European single market in which promising startups can grow.

proj-syn.title: Is Germany’s Firewall Collapsing?
proj-syn.description: After achieving an historic victory in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, the far-right Alternative für Deutschland has just finished first in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, too. Do the results vindicate critics who argue that uniting to keep the AfD out of power is undemocratic and ultimately self-defeating?

proj-syn.title: The Middle Powers Are Now the “Free World”
proj-syn.description: Europe, Canada, and the democracies of Africa, Asia, and Latin America now bear the burden of keeping the old American ideal of the free world alive. While the ideal was always a noble lie, it enabled hundreds of millions of people to imagine a better world during the Cold War, and it could do so again.

proj-syn.title: What Xi Really Wants From Trump
proj-syn.description: As US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, prepare to meet in Washington, American policymakers must not underestimate China’s ambitions. Under Xi, its foreign policy is focused on securing the support of the Global South while pursuing the long-term goal of seizing Taiwan and achieving global preeminence.

proj-syn.title: Europe in a Multi-Aligned World
proj-syn.description: As the Sino-American rivalry intensifies, Europe may be tempted to position itself as a third pole of geopolitics. But instead of defining its power in relation to a bipolarity that many countries are seeking to escape, the continent should focus on building a new architecture of interdependence in which it occupies a central role.

proj-syn.title: A Central European Model for EU Growth
proj-syn.description: As the European Union struggles to revive growth and loses ground to the United States and China, its economic future looks increasingly uncertain. Central Europe’s experience suggests that reversing that decline will require fostering innovation while helping poorer countries catch up.

proj-syn.title: Might Makes Right Will End Pax Americana
proj-syn.description: Far from bolstering US dominance, Donald Trump’s embrace of coercive militarism has eroded it. When the distinction between war and peace dissolves into a ceasefire that is neither, and months of bombardment fail to deliver anything like victory, force looks less like strength and more like pointless destruction.

proj-syn.title: A Roadmap for the Next UN Secretary-General
proj-syn.description: The next UN secretary-general will take over the most prominent position in multilateral governance at a time when multilateralism is arguably at its nadir. Adapting to today’s multipolar reality will require instilling a renewed sense of purpose and demanding more of member states.

proj-syn.title: A New World Order Is Not Beckoning
proj-syn.description: It does no good to get misty-eyed about the demise of the liberal international “order.” What the world really needs to manage today's biggest risks is a different, more realistic narrative that does not draw a sharp line between a disintegrating ideal and its post-liberal successor.

proj-syn.title: What It Means for Global Warming to Exceed 1.5°C

That means humanity must pivot from simply containing global warming to finding ways to reverse it.
